default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-398.title: Mirror-of-open swing fade
E-398.hypothesis: Day traders anchor on the session open; once the day has dipped well below it, the price an equal distance above the open (the low mirrored through the open) is where those who bought the low book a symmetric profit and open-anchored sellers lean, so a bar that tags the mirror level and closes back below it is faded (and the reverse after a deep high).

E-399.title: Connors RSI extreme fade
E-399.hypothesis: A composite of very short RSI, the RSI of the up/down close streak and the percentile of the last bar's return flags moments when one side has hit the tape several bars in a row with unusually large prints; liquidity providers absorb that one-sided flow and are paid when it pauses, so fade the moment the composite enters its extreme.

E-400.title: Quarter-hour block overreaction fade
E-400.hypothesis: Execution algorithms slice parent orders on a fixed clock; a block of 10 to 20 minutes that moved much more than usual for its time and closed at its own extreme marks a slice that pushed through thin liquidity, and short-horizon returns tend to reverse at that horizon, so fade the block at its close.

E-401.title: VWAP-TWAP gap follow
E-401.hypothesis: When the session's volume-weighted price moves clearly above its time-weighted price, contracts are changing hands mostly at the higher prices of the day, meaning buyers accepted them with size rather than the price merely drifting there; follow the side where the volume has been transacted.

E-402.title: Previous clock-hour floor-pivot fade
E-402.hypothesis: Floor pivots built from the previous clock hour's high, low and close give R1/S1 (or R2/S2) levels that short-term desks quote and rest orders at; a bar that tags the level and closes back inside is met by those resting responsive orders, so fade it back toward the hour's pivot.

E-403.title: First box break after a quiet spell fade
E-403.hypothesis: When no close has escaped the rolling short-term box for a long time the tape is in balance and resting stops accumulate just outside it; the first break after such a spell is usually those stops being run by a small push, after which the balancing participants step back in, so fade it.

E-404.title: Klinger volume-force hook fade
E-404.hypothesis: The Klinger oscillator measures signed volume force; once it has reached an extreme for this market and then turns back inside the band, the aggressive volume that drove the move is spent and the counterparties who absorbed it now hold the better inventory, so fade the move at the hook.

E-405.title: Laguerre RSI hook fade
E-405.hypothesis: Ehlers' Laguerre RSI reacts quickly with little lag; a hook back out of its oversold (overbought) zone shows the short burst of selling (buying) has stopped making progress, and the market makers who absorbed it lean the other way, so trade the hook against the burst.

E-406.title: Two-horizon range-position mismatch fade
E-406.hypothesis: A close at the top of the last 15 to 60 minutes while still in the lower part of a wide day's range is a short-covering bounce inside a weak session: the participants who sold higher still hold the inventory above and sell into it, so fade the local extreme toward the day's side (and the reverse on strong days).

E-407.title: Ultimate Oscillator hook fade
E-407.hypothesis: Williams' Ultimate Oscillator blends buying pressure over three horizons, so an extreme reading means every horizon agrees the move was one-sided; when it turns back out of the extreme the multi-horizon pressure is fading and the absorbing side gets paid, so trade the hook against the move.
